title: Beyond Conversation: Why Documents Transform Natural Language into Code - Filip Kozera
talk_summary: A conceptual talk arguing that chat interfaces suffer from context pollution, concurrency-of-one, and lack of forced clarity, and that structured documents plus triggers are the right substrate for background agents. It proposes humans act as approvers/editors of agent output, with documents encoding intent and taste for repeatable processes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Replace long conversational context with a maintained structured document that specifies the task, so iteration edits one precise sentence rather than polluting a growing context window.

Only after a process is proven repeatable and trusted, write it as a document and attach a trigger (cron, event, implicit signal) so it runs in the background and surfaces only when stuck or needing approval.
Background agents do the bulk work; humans approve, reject, edit output, or fix the agent's logic, progressively building trust.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent can do a bunch of work and we get to approve, reject it, change the way that it's created the end output

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues MCP lacks metadata on an agent's constraints, authority, and whether human approval is required; wants these declared per agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it lacks more information about what are the constraints of a particular agents, what are the authority that it needs

takeaways.what_they_do: Documents force the specifier to answer the clarifying questions chat models fail to ask, making intent explicit before work starts.
